title: M-D092826-03 Implementation Details of NPRR1281 and NPRR1327 (Settlement-related)

documents.text:
Market Notice Details

To:

Notice_PRR_SCR@lists.ercot.com,Notice_Settlements@lists.ercot.com,Notice_CRR@lists.ercot.com,Notice_Operations@lists.ercot.com

Sent:

11/13/26, 8:41 AM

Subject:

M-D092826-03 Implementation Details of NPRR1281 and NPRR1327 (Settlement-related)

NOTICE DATE:
 November 13, 2026

NOTICE TYPE:
 M-D092826-03 NPRR/SCR

SHORT DESCRIPTION:
 Implementation Details of NPRR1281 and NPRR1327 (Settlement-related)

INTENDED AUDIENCE:
 All Market Participants

DAYS AFFECTED:
 November 15, 2026

LONG DESCRIPTION: 
As previously noted in Market Notices 
M-D092826-01
 and 
M-D0928206-02
, 
Settlement-related changes to the Protocols associated with Nodal Protocol Revision Request (NPRR) 1281, Improvements to Alternate FFSS Resource Designation, and NPRR 1327, As-Built for NPRR1281, Improvements to Alternate FFSS Resource Designation, became effective on October 29, 2026.  With the beginning of the Firm Fuel Supply Service (FFSS) Obligation Period, the first Operating Day to utilize these Settlement-related changes will be November 15, 2026.  Qualified Scheduling Entities (QSEs) representing FFSS Resources (FFSSRs) must follow these updated requirements for the upcoming FFSS Obligation Period.

NPRR1281
 and 
NPRR1327
 introduce the following Settlement-related changes to the Protocols:

Section 3.14.5, Firm Fuel Supply Service: Automates how ERCOT determines availability data for the FFSS Hourly Rolling Equivalent Availability Factor (FFSSHREAF) calculation. ERCOT will use the Availability Plan for the primary or any approved alternate Generation Resource providing FFSS. With this automation, QSEs no longer need to email ERCOT when the FFSSR acting as the primary Generation Resource changes, although a call to the control room operator is still required.

Section 6.6.14.2, Firm Fuel Supply Service Hourly Standby Fee Payment and Fuel Replacement Cost Recovery: New paragraph (3) clarifies how ERCOT determines the High Sustained Limit (HSL) when a QSE submits multiple Availability Plans for alternate Generation Resources.

Section 8.1.1.2.1.6, Firm Fuel Supply Service Resource Qualification, Testing, Decertification, and Recertification: Revised paragraph (7) clarifies that a QSE must submit an Availability Plan only for an alternate Generation Resource that was designated in the FFSS Offer Submission Form and only when the QSE intends that Resource to replace the primary as the FFSSR.

ACTION REQUIRED:
 Market Participants with shadow Settlement systems should update them for the Protocol revisions in NPRR1281 and NPRR1327.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

NPRR1281
 and 
NPRR1327
 and the associated documents can be found on the ERCOT website.

ClientServices@ercot.com
